top_strength: The No Worries Damage Coverage explanation was the best moment of the call — he contrasted the $2,000 coverage against the state's 60 cents per pound and made it concrete with the 50-lb TV example ('they'll give you like $30 to repair that'). He also closed hard and well: named the last remaining Sunday slot, led with 'no deposit,' and offered to note the 29th preference on the profile if it opened up, which got the customer to commit on the call.
coaching_note: Add the Save Your Ass prep speech — it is worth 10 points and he scored zero on it. This call was the ideal setup for it: the customer said outright 'we do all of our own packing' and 'it's not gonna take that long to load,' which is the perfect opening to say prep before move day equals a shorter move and a lower bill, then give the consolidation examples (loose drawer items, photos off the walls) and the take-a-carload tip. On a $2,325 estimate that speech directly protects the estimate accuracy number. Second priority: he used 'Ian' exactly once in 11 minutes — using the name three or more times is free points and changes how the call feels.
phone_presence_notes: Warm and natural ('Love to hear it,' 'bud'), and he genuinely reflected the customer's points back ('Gotcha, so it's gonna be much closer to the stairs, is what you're saying'), with the customer ending on 'Amazing' and 'sounds great' — held back from a 5 by a long uninterrupted pricing monologue and near-zero name use.
